items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: So I got a job for a fella by the name of Mike Tinsitore. And he was very interested in my music, and he wanted to give me a job, and he accepted it

ctx.x: Fess, something I guess a lot of people, especially those who aren't from New Orleans, would like to know, WTUL having a lot of student listeners who aren't from around here. How did you ever get the name, Professor Longhair?

Well, when I was dancing, of course, when it began, I was dancing. It was called Whirlwind when I was dancing. And I decided to quit dancing and go into the music field. So I left. From up in the direction where I was staying, went across Canal Street, way down around the Seventh-Oo-Six-Wars. People that didn't know me down there, at that time I was wearing long, long hair. And this is where they would approach me, say, Longhair, what is really your name? And I told them my name, but it didn't do any good,…

It's funny, the first time I think I saw you was at Tulane, so that's very appropriate. Yeah, we have a little bit of Professor and all. Where'd you grow up, what part of town did you grow up in? Were you, you weren't born in New Orleans, were you?
